evals.prompt: Right after shifting pods onto a new AL2023 node group, legacy Python pods that do NOT have IRSA or EKS Pod Identity configured started failing with `botocore.exceptions.NoCredentialsError: Unable to locate credentials`, even though the node IAM role still has the S3 policy attached! expectations: Activates the eks-al2-to-al2023-migration skill

Identifies **IMDSv2 defaults on AL2023**: `HttpTokens = required` and `HttpPutResponseHopLimit = 1` (whereas AL2 allowed IMDSv1 / hop-limit 2), causing bridged non-`hostNetwork` pod packets (which decrement IP TTL by 1 across the container veth bridge) to be dropped at the instance metadata endpoint when hop limit is `1`

Provides both the immediate Launch Template `MetadataOptions` workaround (`HttpPutResponseHopLimit = 2` with `HttpTokens = required`) AND strongly recommends migrating pods off node-role IMDS to **EKS Pod Identity** or **IRSA** so pods do not inherit broad node IAM credentials

evals.prompt: We are migrating 40 microservices from AL2 (`cgroup v1`) to AL2023 (`cgroup v2` unified hierarchy). Several older `openjdk:8u191` and `golang:1.17` containers get `OOMKilled` (`exitCode 137`) within minutes on AL2023 staging nodes because the JVM allocates a 16 GiB heap on a 64 GiB node despite a `2Gi` Kubernetes pod memory limit! Explain why and give the concrete runtime/version remediation checklist.
expectations: Activates the eks-al2-to-al2023-migration skill

Explains that AL2023 exclusively uses **cgroup v2** (`/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max` and `cpu.max`), removing legacy cgroup v1 paths (`/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes`), so older cgroup-v2-unaware JVMs fall back to reading host physical RAM (`64 GiB`) when sizing default heap

Recommends upgrading Java to a cgroup-v2-aware LTS release (`Java 11.0.16+` / `17+` / `21+` with `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage`), upgrading Go (`1.19+` with `GOMEMLIMIT` / `automemlimit`), and auditing `.NET` / Node.js runtimes or legacy monitoring agents reading `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/*`
